text: When you build a REST API, good design matters. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names that show what they do. For example, use /users to get a list of users. Always return the right status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API quickly. It should explain each endpoint, the parameters, and possible responses. Finally, use versioning, such as /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing apps. Following these practices makes your API easier to use and maintain.
